experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Resort Day Pass
experiences.description: Ski the iconic slopes beneath the Matterhorn at one of Switzerland's most famous resorts. With over 360km of marked runs, Zermatt offers world-class skiing for all levels, stunning alpine scenery, and glacier skiing that runs nearly year-round. Rent equipment on-site and take the Gornergrat railway for breathtaking panoramic views between runs.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Jungfrau-Aletsch region on a guided snowshoe trek through pristine alpine wilderness. Trek past frozen waterfalls, through snow-laden pine forests, and across the vast Aletsch Glacier viewpoints. A certified mountain guide leads the 4-hour excursion, providing equipment, safety briefing, and hot chocolate at a mountain hut.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Freestyle Skiing & Snow Park
experiences.description: Hit the world-renowned Corviglia Snow Park in St. Moritz, a playground for freestyle skiers and snowboarders featuring half-pipes, kickers, and rails. St. Moritz hosted two Winter Olympics and the terrain park reflects that elite pedigree. Spend a full day mastering jumps and tricks with optional 2-hour freestyle coaching sessions available on-site.

experiences.name: Verbier Off-Piste Backcountry Skiing with Guide
experiences.description: Experience the legendary off-piste terrain of Verbier with a certified IFMGA mountain guide. Explore untracked powder fields, steep couloirs, and remote backcountry routes across the 4 Vallées ski area. This full-day adventure includes avalanche safety equipment, a beacon check, and a traditional Swiss raclette lunch at a mountain restaurant mid-route.

experiences.name: Davos Ice Skating & Curling at Europe's Largest Natural Ice Rink
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary Davos Eisstadion, Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rink, and try your hand at curling — a beloved Swiss alpine tradition. Rent skates and join a beginner curling lesson led by a local club member. As the sun sets over the surrounding peaks, the rink transforms into a magical twilight experience with warm Glühwein available rinkside.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Davos Ice Skating & Curling at Europe's Largest Natural Ice Rink
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary Davos Eisstadion, Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rink, and try your hand at curling — a beloved Swiss alpine tradition. Rent skates and join a beginner curling lesson led by a local club member. As the sun sets over the surrounding peaks, the rink transforms into a magical twilight experience with warm Glühwein available rinkside.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at destination airport at 13:00. Take the most budget-friendly train route to Zermatt (trains run regularly from Zurich/Geneva airports via Visp to Zermatt — book Swiss Travel Pass or point-to-point tickets in advance for savings). Check in to Valais Boutique Stay in Zermatt. Drop luggage, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll through the car-free village of Zermatt to get oriented. Admire the iconic Matterhorn views from the village and scout the ski rental shops for the best budget deals on equipment rental for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zermatt's main street (Bahnhofstrasse) on foot. Visit the free Matterhorn Museum Zermatlantis entrance area for a quick cultural introduction (full entry ~CHF 10 if budget allows). Watch the sunset alpenglow on the Matterhorn from the village — completely free and breathtaking.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick pastry and coffee at the airport arrival hall (~CHF 5–8)
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or wrap from a Migros or Coop supermarket at the train station en route (~CHF 6–9)
meals.dinner: Walliserkanne Restaurant in Zermatt — order the budget-friendly Raclette or Käseschnitte (cheese toast), a Swiss classic (~CHF 18–22). Alternatively, pick up groceries at the local Coop in Zermatt for a self-catered dinner (~CHF 10–14)

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — all transport within the village is by electric taxi or on foot. Buy a Swiss Travel Pass online before departure for significant savings on trains. Rent ski equipment on Day 1 evening to save time on Day 2 morning. Book ski passes at the Zermatt Matterhorn ski resort ticket office or online for multi-day discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Full first ski day on the Zermatt Matterhorn ski area — one of the largest ski resorts in the Alps with 360km of runs. Start early (lifts open ~08:30) to avoid crowds. Beginners should head to the Sunnegga Paradise area (accessible via underground funicular); intermediate/advanced skiers head to Rothorn or Gornergrat sectors. Purchase a budget day ski pass (~CHF 75–85 for adults; look for online early-bird discounts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the afternoon. Take a break at a mid-mountain self-service restaurant such as Sunnegga Restaurant for a lighter, cheaper meal. Explore the runs connecting to the Italian border at Cervinia for stunning cross-border scenery (note: crossing into Italy requires a bi-national pass upgrade — skip if on tight budget). Return skis and gear to locker by 16:30.
day_by_day.evening: Relax tired muscles with a free soak in the natural mountain air. Walk along the Gorner Gorge trail near the village (free access in winter, check local conditions). Browse the village shops and enjoy a warm drink at a café.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — buy bread, cheese, and yogurt from Coop the night before (~CHF 4–6)
meals.lunch: Self-service cafeteria at Sunnegga mountain restaurant — soup and bread or a simple hot dish (~CHF 14–18)
meals.dinner: Snowboat Bar & Restaurant in Zermatt — known for affordable burgers and hearty mountain food (~CHF 18–24). Or self-cater from Coop supermarket (~CHF 10–14)

day_by_day.notes: Multi-day ski passes (3-day, 6-day) offer significant per-day savings — consider buying a 6-day pass upfront (~CHF 340–380) if you plan to ski most days. Rent equipment from Sport Julen or Slalom Sport in Zermatt for competitive budget rates. Dress in warm layers — February temperatures at altitude can drop to -10°C to -15°C.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway (included in Swiss Travel Pass or ~CHF 44 return) up to 3,089m for one of the most spectacular panoramic views in the Alps — a sweeping vista of 29 four-thousand-metre peaks including the Matterhorn, Monte Rosa, and Lyskamm. Spend time at the Kulmhotel Gornergrat observation terrace photographing the scenery. This is a non-skiing morning focused on the mountain experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski or snowboard down from Gornergrat back toward the village through the Riffelberg and Riffelalp sectors — a long, scenic descent of over 1,400m vertical drop. Stop at the free Riffelsee lake viewpoint where, on calm days, the Matterhorn reflects perfectly in the frozen lake. Return to village by 15:30 and return rental equipment if taking a rest day tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free weekly torchlight descent event (check local Zermatt tourism calendar — typically held on Wednesday or Friday evenings in winter). Local ski instructors ski down the mountain with flaming torches — a spectacular free show visible from the village. Afterward, warm up with a Glühwein (mulled wine) from a village stall (~CHF 5–7).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — oatmeal, fruit, and coffee (~CHF 3–5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Coop — sandwich, fruit, and hot tea in a thermos to enjoy at the Gornergrat summit (~CHF 7–9)
meals.dinner: Restaurant du Pont in Zermatt — traditional Swiss fondue (book ahead, minimum 2 people, ~CHF 22–28 per person). Budget tip: split a fondue pot between travel companions

day_by_day.notes: The Gornergrat railway is one of Switzerland's most iconic train journeys — book tickets the evening before or early morning to secure a window seat. Bring sunscreen even in February — UV radiation is intense at high altitude. The torchlight descent schedule is posted at the Zermatt tourist office and on the Zermatt.ch website.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day from skiing. Take a free self-guided winter hiking trail from the village — the Zermatt Winter Hiking Network offers over 50km of maintained paths. The Sunnegga–Findeln–Zermatt trail is a beautiful easy-to-moderate 2-hour walk through snow-covered forests with constant Matterhorn views. Wear waterproof boots and warm layers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Matterhorn Museum Zermatlantis (full entry ~CHF 10) to learn about the first ascent of the Matterhorn in 1865 and the history of Zermatt as a mountain village. Afterward, explore the old village quarter ('Hinterdorf') with its ancient wooden mazots (raised grain storehouses) — a free and photogenic cultural walk. Stop at the English Church (free entry), the oldest Anglican church in the Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Try snowshoeing on a budget-friendly evening snowshoe tour — Zermatt offers guided group snowshoe tours from ~CHF 35 per person including equipment rental. Alternatively, rent snowshoes independently (~CHF 15–20) and explore the lit winter trails near the village independently after dark.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs, toast, and juice at accommodation (~CHF 4–6)
meals.lunch: Café du Pont or Elsie's Bar in Zermatt — soup of the day and bread, a warming budget lunch (~CHF 12–16)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hot meal at accommodation using groceries from Coop — pasta with Swiss cheese sauce or rösti (Swiss potato dish) (~CHF 8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is intentionally a rest day to prevent muscle fatigue and reduce injury risk for the remaining ski days. The Matterhorn Museum is highly recommended and excellent value. Check the Zermatt tourism office for any free evening events, concerts, or ski film screenings that may be scheduled this week.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by train to Davos (approximately 3–3.5 hours via Visp, Chur, Landquart — check SBB timetable; covered by Swiss Travel Pass or ~CHF 40–55 return). Arrive in Davos by mid-morning. Head directly to the legendary Davos Eisstadion — Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rink. Rent ice skates (~CHF 7–10) and skate on the iconic open-air rink surrounded by mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try curling at the Davos Eisstadion — group curling sessions are available for beginners (~CHF 15–20 per person including equipment and brief instruction). This is a fun, social Swiss winter sport experience. Afterward, explore the Davos Promenade and take in views of the Davos valley. If time and budget allow, consider a short ski session at the Parsenn ski area in Davos (~CHF 65–75 day pass).
day_by_day.evening: Return train to Zermatt (approximately 3–3.5 hours). Arrive back in Zermatt by 20:00–21:00. Enjoy a quiet evening at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure — bread, cheese, and coffee (~CHF 4–6)
meals.lunch: Davos Eisstadion café or nearby Migros supermarket in Davos — budget lunch of soup, sandwich, or daily special (~CHF 10–15)
meals.dinner: Grab a takeaway Döner or pizza slice from a village snack bar in Zermatt upon return (~CHF 10–14)

day_by_day.notes: The Davos day trip is a long travel day — depart Zermatt no later than 07:30 to maximize time at the ice rink. Davos Eisstadion is typically open from late November to late February/early March depending on temperatures. Confirm opening hours at davos.ch before departure. The Swiss Travel Pass covers the entire train journey — a major cost saver.

day_by_day.morning: Final full ski day — make the most of the Zermatt ski area. Head to the Schwarzsee sector (accessible via cable car from village) for intermediate and advanced terrain with some of the best Matterhorn close-up views on the mountain. Push yourself to try a new run or sector you haven't skied yet this week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Klein Matterhorn sector (accessible via cable car to 3,883m — the highest cable car station in the Alps). On clear days, views extend across the Alps into France and Italy. This is a bucket-list alpine experience. Ski back down via the long Theodul Glacier run. Return to village by 15:30 and return all rental equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the final evening in Zermatt with a budget splurge dinner. Visit the Zermatt Unplugged acoustic music festival area if it overlaps with your dates (usually April — check calendar), or enjoy live music at one of the village après-ski bars. Walk to the Matterhorn viewpoint near the cemetery for a final nighttime view of the illuminated peak.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — hearty porridge, nuts, banana, and coffee for energy before skiing (~CHF 4–6)
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant self-service at Trockener Steg or Schwarzsee — daily soup special and bread (~CHF 14–18)
meals.dinner: Budget splurge at Whymper-Stube in Zermatt — named after Edward Whymper who first climbed the Matterhorn; hearty Swiss mountain cuisine, fondues and raclette (~CHF 25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically the busiest day on the slopes as weekly ski chalet guests arrive — head to the lifts early (08:00–08:30) to beat queues. Return all rental equipment by 17:00 to avoid late fees. Pack bags in the evening for the departure day tomorrow. Keep receipts — some ski rental shops offer a small refund for early returns.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Valais Boutique Stay. Store luggage at the hotel or at Zermatt train station left-luggage lockers (~CHF 5–8). Take one final walk through the village and up to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise viewpoint area (if time allows before train departure) or simply enjoy a slow farewell coffee with Matterhorn views from a village café. Visit the Zermatt tourist market on the main street for affordable Swiss souvenirs — local cheese, chocolate, and postcards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the train from Zermatt toward your departure airport (Zurich or Geneva). The journey takes approximately 3.5–4 hours to Zurich or 3 hours to Geneva. Use the scenic train ride to reflect on the week and enjoy the passing Swiss landscape. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. If flight is late evening, use airport time to enjoy a final Swiss chocolate purchase from the duty-free shops (often cheaper than village prices). Board your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at accommodation or a farewell coffee and croissant at a Zermatt café (~CHF 6–10)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or Migros/Coop station sandwich for the train journey (~CHF 7–10)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or grab-and-go option at the departure terminal (~CHF 15–20)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — confirm with the hotel. Buy any last-minute Swiss chocolate or cheese at Coop in Zermatt (significantly cheaper than airport prices). Validate Swiss Travel Pass for the return journey if applicable. Keep all ski lift tickets as some resorts offer refunds for unused days due to weather or injury — check Zermatt resort policy. Budget summary for the week: accommodation + ski passes + transport + food should total approximately CHF 800–1,100 per person if planned carefully.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Upon landing, collect luggage and take the scenic Glacier Express or train connection from Zurich/Geneva airport to Zermatt (approximately 3–4 hours). Enjoy the stunning alpine scenery through the train window as you wind through mountain valleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at Boutique Stay in Zermatt, Valais. After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through Zermatt's charming car-free village center. Visit the Bahnhofstrasse for a first glimpse of the Matterhorn, explore local ski shops to rent or tune equipment for the days ahead, and get oriented with the resort map.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and acclimatize to the mountain altitude. Take a short walk to the Gornergrat viewpoint area for a stunning twilight view of the Matterhorn. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a cozy local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on the train — try the onboard dining car for a Swiss-style snack.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the train station or onboard; alternatively, grab a quick bite at Zermatt Bahnhof café upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Whymper-Stube, a mid-range Zermatt classic known for fondue and raclette — perfect Swiss mountain welcome meal. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — use the electric taxi or hotel shuttle from the Zermatt train station. Rent ski equipment tonight or first thing tomorrow morning to save time. Stay hydrated as Zermatt sits at 1,620m elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Resort Day Pass — Hit the iconic slopes beneath the Matterhorn on your first full ski day. Start with the Gornergrat cable car or Sunnegga Express for breathtaking morning runs on groomed pistes. The early morning light on the Matterhorn is spectacular. Beginner to intermediate skiers should explore the Sunnegga–Blauherd area, while advanced skiers can head toward Klein Matterhorn (3,883m) for high-altitude runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing the Zermatt ski area, exploring the Rothorn or Schwarzsee sectors. Take a mid-afternoon break at one of the mountain restaurants on the slopes. Try the famous Chez Vrony or Bergrestaurant Sunnegga for a mountain lunch with Matterhorn views. Return skis and equipment to the valley by 16:30.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at the Hennu Stall or Papperla Pub — a classic Zermatt tradition. Then head back to the hotel to freshen up before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local bakery such as Bäckerei Fuchs — fresh bread, Swiss müesli, and coffee. Budget CHF 10–18.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the slopes — try rösti with cheese or a hearty soup at Bergrestaurant Sunnegga. Budget CHF 20–30.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Myoko or Pizzeria Roma in Zermatt village — relaxed mid-range dining with pasta, pizza, or Swiss dishes. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Zermatt ski pass in advance online for a small discount. The Klein Matterhorn sector connects to Cervinia, Italy — bring your passport if you want to ski across the border. Wear high SPF sunscreen at altitude even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Off-Piste Backcountry Skiing with Guide — Take an early morning train or transfer to Verbier (approximately 2–2.5 hours via Le Châble). Meet your certified IFMGA mountain guide for a full-day backcountry adventure. Explore Verbier's legendary off-piste terrain including the famous Mont-Fort area. The guide will assess snow conditions and choose the safest, most exhilarating routes through untracked powder.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the backcountry skiing experience with your guide through the afternoon, exploring couloirs and wide open powder fields in the Verbier–Four Valleys region. The guide will lead you through terrain inaccessible to regular resort skiers, providing an unforgettable alpine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt by early evening train. Rest and recover with a relaxing soak or spa treatment at the hotel if available, or simply enjoy a quiet evening in the village.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — Swiss-style continental with cold cuts, cheese, and bread.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or mountain hut stop arranged through the guide — typically a rustic mountain refuge (cabane) with hot soup and bread included or at low cost.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Gitan in Zermatt — a beloved local restaurant with excellent raclette, fondue, and grilled meats in a warm chalet atmosphere. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Verbier backcountry guide well in advance as they fill up quickly in peak season. Ensure you have appropriate avalanche safety gear (beacon, probe, shovel) — your guide will confirm what to bring. This is a full-day excursion; comfortable return to Zermatt by 19:00–20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking — Take the train from Zermatt toward Interlaken/Grindelwald (approximately 3 hours via Visp). Join a guided snowshoe trek through the UNESCO World Heritage Jungfrau-Aletsch region. The guide leads you through pristine winter landscapes with views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Perfect for a rest day from intense skiing while still enjoying the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoe trek through the afternoon, exploring snow-covered forests and open alpine meadows. Optional: visit the Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe (3,454m) by cogwheel railway for panoramic views of the longest glacier in the Alps. Return to Interlaken by late afternoon and travel back to Zermatt.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Zermatt by evening. Enjoy a relaxed evening strolling the village, browsing local shops for Swiss souvenirs or chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before the early train departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mountain restaurant in the Jungfrau region — try the Bergrestaurant Grindelwald First or a cozy hut along the snowshoe trail. Budget CHF 20–35.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Stockhorn in Zermatt — mid-range Swiss cuisine with excellent fondue bourguignonne and local wines. Budget CHF 30–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe rentals are available at the Grindelwald or Wengen sports shops if not included in the tour. The Jungfraujoch add-on costs approximately CHF 100–145 and is worth booking in advance. This day involves significant train travel — consider a Swiss Travel Pass for savings.

day_by_day.morning: St. Moritz Freestyle Skiing & Snow Park — Take the scenic Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz (approximately 7.5 hours, one of the world's most beautiful train journeys) — OR take a faster regional connection via Chur (approximately 4–5 hours). Arrive in St. Moritz and head directly to the Corviglia Snow Park. Warm up with park features including jumps, rails, and boxes suited for all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Corviglia Snow Park and the wider Engadin ski area. St. Moritz offers world-class groomed pistes in addition to the park. Try the famous Hahnensee run or explore the Corvatsch and Diavolezza sectors for varied terrain. Rent freestyle-specific skis or a snowboard from the resort if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Experience St. Moritz's glamorous après-ski scene — visit the Caprices or Roo Bar for a drink. Overnight in St. Moritz at a mid-range guesthouse or hotel (pre-booked) as it is too far to return to Zermatt the same evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the Glacier Express train or at the Zermatt station café before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mathis Food Affairs or a mountain restaurant on Corviglia — stunning lake views over the Engadin valley. Budget CHF 25–40.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pizzeria Caruso or Restaurant Veltlinerkeller in St. Moritz — excellent mid-range Italian and Swiss options in the village. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This day requires an overnight stay in St. Moritz — book a mid-range hotel such as Hotel Languard or Hotel Bellaval in advance. Budget CHF 120–200 per night. The Glacier Express is highly recommended for the scenery but book seats in advance. Alternatively, fly or take a faster train connection.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Ice Skating & Curling at Europe's Largest Natural Ice Rink — Travel from St. Moritz to Davos by PostBus or train (approximately 1.5–2 hours via Filisur). Arrive at the legendary Davos Eisstadion — Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rink. Rent ice skates and enjoy a morning session on the iconic rink surrounded by mountain scenery. Then try your hand at curling — a quintessential Swiss winter activity with instruction available for beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Davos town and the Parsenn ski area for a few afternoon runs if energy allows — Davos–Klosters offers excellent intermediate skiing. Alternatively, visit the Davos Congress Centre area for a cultural break, or simply enjoy a relaxed walk along the frozen Davosersee lake. Begin the return journey to Zermatt via train (approximately 3.5–4 hours via Chur and Visp).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at your Boutique Stay in Zermatt. Enjoy a final relaxing evening in the village — perhaps a nightcap at one of Zermatt's cozy bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your St. Moritz accommodation before checkout.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Davos Eisstadion café or a nearby restaurant in Davos — try a Swiss wurst with rösti or a warming Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup). Budget CHF 18–28.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Julen's restaurant or Restaurant Zum See in Zermatt — a beloved mountain restaurant known for its rustic charm and excellent Swiss cuisine. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Davos Eisstadion is open weather permitting — natural ice depends on temperatures staying below freezing. Skate rental is approximately CHF 8–12. Curling sessions can be booked on-site. Keep an eye on train schedules to ensure a comfortable return to Zermatt by evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final Ski Day at Zermatt — Make the most of your last morning with a final run on the Zermatt slopes. Head up on the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car for one last iconic view from 3,883m — the highest cable car station in the Alps. Take photos of the Matterhorn in the clear morning light and enjoy a few leisurely runs down to the valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the village by midday. Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the hotel or station. Spend the afternoon exploring Zermatt's village shops — pick up Swiss chocolate, cheese, or a Matterhorn souvenir. Visit the Alpine Museum (Alpines Museum der Schweiz) for a brief cultural insight into Zermatt's mountaineering history.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Zermatt village before departing or resting for an early morning departure. Reflect on an incredible week in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy the full Swiss spread of müesli, cheese, cold cuts, fresh bread, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café du Pont or a local bakery in Zermatt village — sandwich, soup, or a slice of Swiss tart. Budget CHF 15–25.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Schäferstube in the Hotel Julen or Chez Heini — enjoy a celebratory cheese fondue or raclette to close out the trip in true Swiss style. Budget CHF 40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check train times from Zermatt to Zurich or Geneva airport for your return journey — the trip takes approximately 3.5–4 hours. Book train tickets in advance for the best prices. Leave enough time for airport check-in. Consider purchasing Swiss chocolate and Gruyère cheese as gifts at the Zermatt Migros or Coop supermarket for budget-friendly souvenirs.

A certified mountain guide leads the 4-hour excursion, providing equipment, safety briefing, and hot chocolate at a mountain hut.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Freestyle Skiing & Snow Park
experiences.description: Hit the world-renowned Corviglia Snow Park in St. Moritz, a playground for freestyle skiers and snowboarders featuring half-pipes, kickers, and rails. St. Moritz hosted two Winter Olympics and the terrain park reflects that elite pedigree. Spend a full day mastering jumps and tricks with optional 2-hour freestyle coaching sessions available on-site.

experiences.name: Verbier Off-Piste Backcountry Skiing with Guide
experiences.description: Experience the legendary off-piste terrain of Verbier with a certified IFMGA mountain guide. Explore untracked powder fields, steep couloirs, and remote backcountry routes across the 4 Vallées ski area. This full-day adventure includes avalanche safety equipment, a beacon check, and a traditional Swiss raclette lunch at a mountain restaurant mid-route.

experiences.name: Davos Ice Skating & Curling at Europe's Largest Natural Ice Rink
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary Davos Eisstadion, Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rink, and try your hand at curling — a beloved Swiss alpine tradition. Rent skates and join a beginner curling lesson led by a local club member. As the sun sets over the surrounding peaks, the rink transforms into a magical twilight experience with warm Glühwein available rinkside.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, a pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you from the airport to Zermatt. Note: Zermatt is car-free, so your driver will take you to Täsch where a private cogwheel train or helicopter transfer completes the journey into the village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in & Village Orientation — Arrive at your Boutique Stay in Zermatt, Valais and complete a leisurely check-in. Spend the afternoon settling in, unpacking, and taking a relaxed stroll through Zermatt's charming car-free village streets. Visit the iconic Bahnhofstrasse, browse luxury ski boutiques (Bogner, Kjus), and get your first breathtaking views of the Matterhorn. Stop by the ski rental shop to arrange premium equipment fitting for the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome Dinner — Enjoy a celebratory welcome dinner at one of Zermatt's finest establishments. Head to Restaurant Chez Vrony on the slopes or the elegant After Seven restaurant for a refined Swiss-French menu featuring local Valais wines and seasonal alpine ingredients.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light snack at Zurich Airport's SWISS Business Lounge or grab a charcuterie board and local cheese platter at a Zermatt café upon arrival
meals.dinner: Restaurant After Seven (Zermatt) — 5-course tasting menu with Valais wine pairing; alternatively, Chez Vrony for fondue and raclette with panoramic Matterhorn views

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange luxury transfer well in advance. Zermatt is strictly car-free — all luggage is transported via electric taxi from Täsch. Confirm ski rental and lift pass reservations for Day 2 upon check-in. The hotel concierge can arrange all bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Resort Day Pass — Hit the slopes early for the best snow conditions. With your premium Zermatt ski pass, access over 360 km of groomed runs across Zermatt and Cervinia (Italy). Start with the iconic Rothorn and Stockhorn sectors for challenging red and black runs with jaw-dropping Matterhorn vistas. A private ski instructor can be arranged through the hotel for a personalized morning session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Skiing — Explore the Klein Matterhorn sector (3,883 m), the highest ski area in the Alps. Take the Matterhorn Glacier Ride cable car for panoramic views across four countries. Ski the legendary 'Matterhorn glacier paradise' black runs before cruising back down to the village on the scenic Weisse Perle run. Enjoy a mid-afternoon break at a mountain restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Après-Ski & Gourmet Dinner — Wind down at the Vernissage Bar or Papperla Pub for classic Zermatt après-ski. Then freshen up for dinner at the Michelin-starred Restaurant Capri at the Grand Hotel Zermatterhof, featuring Italian-alpine cuisine with an exceptional wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast at your boutique hotel — freshly baked bread, local cheeses, cold cuts, bircher muesli, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Restaurant Findlerhof (mid-mountain) — renowned for its stunning Matterhorn terrace, truffle pasta, and Swiss rösti with mountain herbs
meals.dinner: Restaurant Capri at Grand Hotel Zermatterhof — Michelin-starred Italian-alpine tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructor through the Swiss Ski School Zermatt at least 48 hours in advance. Start skiing by 08:30 to enjoy fresh groomed pistes before crowds. Apply high-SPF glacier sunscreen — UV radiation is intense at altitude. Zermatt-Cervinia cross-border skiing requires a valid passport.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Off-Piste Backcountry Skiing with Guide — Depart early via private transfer to Verbier (approximately 1.5 hours from Zermatt). Meet your certified IFMGA mountain guide for an exclusive off-piste backcountry skiing experience. Explore Verbier's legendary untracked powder fields, hidden couloirs, and remote terrain in the Mont Fort sector. Safety equipment (avalanche transceiver, probe, shovel) is provided. This is a world-class experience for confident intermediate-to-advanced skiers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Verbier Exploration & Skiing — After the guided backcountry session, enjoy a few runs on Verbier's groomed pistes in the 4 Vallées ski area (412 km of runs). Ride the Mont Fort cable car to 3,330 m for spectacular views of the Grand Combin and Mont Blanc massifs. Optional: try a helicopter ski drop for an additional premium surcharge.
day_by_day.evening: Return & Relaxed Evening — Private transfer back to Zermatt. After a physically demanding day, enjoy the hotel's spa facilities — sauna, steam room, and hot tub. A lighter, intimate dinner at a cozy local restaurant rounds out the evening.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast at 07:00 — high-energy options including eggs, smoked salmon, granola, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Vache in Verbier — iconic mountain restaurant known for its Angus beef burgers, tartiflette, and lively atmosphere with Mont Blanc views
meals.dinner: Le Mazot Restaurant, Zermatt — intimate chalet-style restaurant specializing in Valais beef fondue, lamb rack, and local Fendant white wine

day_by_day.notes: Verbier off-piste skiing requires a minimum intermediate-advanced skill level. The IFMGA guide will assess conditions and adjust the route for safety. Wear moisture-wicking base layers and pack energy snacks. Confirm private transfer timing the evening before. Return to Zermatt by approximately 18:00.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking — Private transfer to the Jungfrau region (approximately 2 hours). Join a guided snowshoe trek through the UNESCO World Heritage Jungfrau-Aletsch landscape. Explore pristine snow-covered forests, frozen alpine meadows, and dramatic glacier viewpoints. The guide shares insights into the region's geology, flora, and alpine traditions. Routes are tailored to your fitness level — options range from leisurely scenic walks to more challenging high-altitude treks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe — Take the legendary Jungfrau Railway to Jungfraujoch (3,454 m), the highest railway station in Europe. Visit the Ice Palace (carved entirely within the Aletsch Glacier), the Sphinx Observatory, and enjoy panoramic views across the longest glacier in the Alps. Explore at your own pace before descending back to Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt & Wellness Evening — Private transfer back to Zermatt. This evening is dedicated to recovery and relaxation. Enjoy a private in-room spa treatment (hot stone massage or alpine herb body wrap) arranged by the hotel concierge. A curated room service dinner with fine Valais wines completes the perfect recovery evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — lighter fare recommended before snowshoeing: yogurt parfait, seasonal fruit, whole grain toast, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Restaurant Grindelwaldblick (Jungfrau region) — traditional Swiss lunch with Älplermagronen (alpine mac and cheese), Appenzeller cheese soup, and local apple strudel
meals.dinner: In-room private dining — curated 3-course menu prepared by the hotel kitchen: Valais asparagus velouté, pan-seared lake trout, dark chocolate fondant with Valais raspberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoeing is suitable for all fitness levels — no prior experience required. Wear waterproof boots and warm layered clothing. The Jungfraujoch visit requires advance ticket booking (sold out weeks ahead in peak season). Altitude at Jungfraujoch can cause mild headaches — stay hydrated and ascend slowly. The hotel concierge should arrange all transfers and tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: St. Moritz Freestyle Skiing & Snow Park — Early private transfer to St. Moritz (approximately 3 hours via scenic mountain roads or faster by helicopter). Arrive at the world-renowned Corviglia Snow Park — a playground for freestyle enthusiasts featuring kickers, rails, halfpipe, and slope-style features. Whether you're a seasoned freestyler or a curious beginner, a professional freestyle coach is on hand for personalized instruction. The park's immaculate grooming and high-altitude setting make this an unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Moritz Village & Lake Experience — After the snow park session, explore the glamorous St. Moritz village — the birthplace of alpine winter tourism. Browse luxury boutiques on Via Serlas (Cartier, Bulgari, Hermès). Take a horse-drawn carriage ride across the frozen St. Moritz Lake, a quintessential Engadin experience. Optional: watch the famous White Turf horse racing on the frozen lake if timing aligns.
day_by_day.evening: St. Moritz Gala Dinner — Dine at one of St. Moritz's legendary establishments before returning to Zermatt. The evening celebrates the trip's midpoint in true St. Moritz style — glamorous, indulgent, and unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast in Zermatt — power breakfast: smoked salmon bagel, poached eggs, fresh juice, and double espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mathis Food Affairs (Corviglia mountain restaurant) — celebrity-frequented mountain eatery with panoramic Engadin views; try the lobster bisque and truffle risotto
meals.dinner: Restaurant Ecco St. Moritz (2 Michelin stars) — avant-garde alpine cuisine by Chef Rolf Fliegauf; exceptional tasting menu with wine pairing featuring rare Swiss and European labels

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter transfer option (Zermatt to St. Moritz, ~30 minutes) is available at a premium surcharge and offers spectacular aerial views of the Swiss Alps — highly recommended for a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Book the freestyle coach through Ski School St. Moritz in advance. Return transfer to Zermatt departs at approximately 20:00 after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Ice Skating & Curling — Private transfer to Davos (approximately 2.5 hours). Visit the legendary Davos Eisstadion — Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rink. Begin with a graceful morning skating session on the vast frozen expanse surrounded by mountain peaks. Then transition to a private curling lesson — a traditional Swiss sport that combines strategy, teamwork, and precision. A dedicated curling coach guides you through the basics with plenty of humor and local tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Davos Skiing & Parsenn Resort — After the ice activities, head to the Parsenn ski area — one of Switzerland's largest and most celebrated ski resorts. Enjoy wide, well-groomed runs with spectacular views of the Graubünden Alps. The legendary Weissfluhjoch to Küblis run (12 km) is one of the longest ski descents in the Alps — an absolute must. Alternatively, explore the quieter Jakobshorn sector popular with freestyle enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt & Farewell Pre-Dinner Drinks — Private transfer back to Zermatt. Gather for pre-dinner cocktails at the Hotel Alex's elegant bar or the sophisticated Vernissage lounge. Enjoy a refined penultimate evening dinner at one of Zermatt's top tables.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Swiss spread with an emphasis on warm dishes: scrambled eggs with truffle, rösti, fresh pastries, and Valais honey
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Weissfluhjoch (Davos) — panoramic mountain restaurant at 2,662 m; enjoy fondue chinoise, mountain charcuterie, and warm Glühwein
meals.dinner: Restaurant Zum See, Zermatt — legendary alpine restaurant accessible only on foot or by ski (summer) in a stunning forest clearing; famous for its seasonal game dishes, homemade pasta, and extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Zum See restaurant requires advance reservations — often booked weeks ahead. The Parsenn ski pass is separate from the Zermatt pass — arrange through the hotel concierge. Davos is at 1,560 m elevation, offering reliable snow conditions. The Weissfluhjoch to Küblis run requires a return train ticket back up — factor this into afternoon timing.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning Skiing in Zermatt — Make the most of your last morning on the iconic Zermatt slopes. Return to your favorite runs or explore any sectors you haven't yet visited — perhaps the scenic Schwarzsee area with its direct Matterhorn views, or the long cruising runs of the Gornergrat sector. Ski until approximately 11:30, then return equipment and collect lift pass refunds if applicable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Zermatt Village Farewell & Souvenir Shopping — Spend your final afternoon savoring Zermatt at a leisurely pace. Visit the Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) for a fascinating insight into the village's mountaineering history. Browse premium Swiss souvenirs — handcrafted watches, Valais wines, local cheeses, and artisan chocolates. Enjoy a final hot chocolate at a cozy café with Matterhorn views. Begin packing and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Gala Dinner & Departure Preparation — Celebrate an extraordinary week with a grand farewell dinner at Zermatt's finest venue. Reflect on the week's adventures over a multi-course tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings. After dinner, the hotel concierge arranges your private luxury transfer to Täsch and onward to the airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Champagne farewell breakfast at the hotel — full luxury spread with Moët & Chandon Brut, eggs Benedict, smoked Valais salmon, artisan croissants, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café du Pont, Zermatt — warm soup, artisan sandwiches, and a glass of local Valais Pinot Noir on the sunny terrace
meals.dinner: Restaurant The Omnia, Zermatt — spectacular cliff-top restaurant with floor-to-ceiling Matterhorn views; 6-course farewell tasting menu featuring the finest Swiss and European produce with Grand Cru wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange departure transfer the evening before — allow at least 3 hours from Zermatt village to Zurich Airport including the Täsch transfer. The hotel concierge can store luggage during the final morning ski session. Consider purchasing a selection of Valais AOC wines and Swiss chocolates as gifts — the hotel can arrange vacuum-packed and airline-approved packaging. Ensure all ski rental equipment is returned by 12:00 to avoid additional charges.
